public_commands.LASEROUT: The sole conversion command. Creates grouped open zero-width LWPOLYLINE glyphs and one orientation key.
public_commands.LASERFONT: Selects the LaserFont3 display style and sets the default text height to 5.

mtext_reproduction.input: Plain lowercase ASCII alphanumeric, single-line, top-left attached MTEXT using a Standard style whose verified font is laserfont3.shx, with no key prefix.
mtext_reproduction.fixture_dependency_note: ObjectDBX copying into a new database retained its pre-existing Standard style font. Only the private unsaved test copy was restored to the independently verified source SHX font before testing; all original MTEXT content, placement, width, attachment and height were retained.
mtext_reproduction.previous_installed_behavior_reproduced: The previous runtime rejected the same restored-font MTEXT solely because its text had no leading key marker.

undo_verification.tested: The real LASEROUT command followed by one U restores the copied MTEXT and all four rotated legacy/v3 TEXT cases, removing their paths and conversion group.
undo_verification.harness_configuration: Automatic command/script Undo grouping disabled in the isolated test profile before each suite.

prior_release_evidence_not_rerun.scope_note: Historical regression evidence for the previous hash only; retired aliases and the former missing-prefix rejection are superseded and are not current acceptance criteria.

limitations: This suite does not verify GUI APPLOAD, the active drawing or the installed candidate; those require separate installation/live proof.

Native MTEXT proof covers the reproduced plain single-line top-left case. Wrapping, columns, inline formatting and unsupported style overrides remain guarded; this suite is not general MTEXT acceptance.
Cancellation, save/reopen, internal exact-curve helpers and arbitrary UCS transforms were not rerun for this candidate. Previous-release proof is recorded separately.
CAM import, physical cutting, kerf, piercing and human orientation recognition were not tested.
Label geometry does not establish the true outside face of a fabricated assembly.
